extracted.intended_audience: administrators, managers and policymakers of unemployment insurance programs; UIC office staff and researchers in public administration
extracted.subtask_short: UIC office procedures and claimant information
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and operational guidelines for organizing UIC (unemployment insurance) offices, informing claimants, processing applications, and allocating decision-making responsibilities among front-line staff (Agents I and II).

rubrics_metrics.name: District Office organizational structure
rubrics_metrics.description: District Offices are headed by a manager supported by three senior assistants; key divisions include Chief of Operations (in charge of officers making decisions concerning claims), Chief of Benefit Control (ensuring claimant compliance), Chief of Administrative Services (personnel, accounting, records, supplies), a general information service, and an insurance division providing technical support and review. Two specialist outward-oriented officers report directly to the manager (public relations and labour market analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes managerial roles and the major divisions that should exist in a fully functioning District Office and their responsibilities for claims processing, compliance, technical support and public liaison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type 1 (District Office)
rubrics_metrics.description: Type 1 is the standard District Office described above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In metropolitan centres a variant (Type IM) may centralize certain technical services but is indistinguishable from Type 1 from the public's point of view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type IM (metropolitan variant)
rubrics_metrics.description: A metropolitan variant of the District Office where the proximity of multiple District Offices makes centralization of some technical services feasible; to claimants this is indistinguishable from a Type 1 office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in urban areas to pool technical functions while keeping service appearance uniform to claimants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type 2 local offices (simplified District Office)
rubrics_metrics.description: A simplified version of the District Office where administrative services are provided by the office to which they are attached; services provided to claimants are the same as in District Offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate for second offices in large cities or polycentric regions where full duplication of administrative infrastructure is not justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type 3A offices (service-oriented, retain files)
rubrics_metrics.description: Offices with functions directly connected to claimant service: typically one service unit (reduced staff) plus minimum benefit control staff; they retain complete claimant files and have a permanent clientele.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes higher-ranked local offices from lower-ranked outlets by retention of claimant files and more permanent service relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type 3B offices (limited initial processing, no files)
rubrics_metrics.description: Offices with reduced staff that retain capability for initial claim processing in straightforward cases but do not keep claim files; early intervention by the District Office is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suitable for locations that can handle simple claims but must escalate more complex or file-dependent matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type 4 offices (part-time collection sites)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part-time 'pied-a-terre' offices where one or more officers visit regularly to collect applications for benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Especially suitable in thinly-populated or rural areas where permanent staff cannot be justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type 5 offices (minimal UIC presence in CMCs)
rubrics_metrics.description: A minimal UIC presence, taking the form of an unemployment insurance information service normally established in Canada Manpower Centres (per sec. 13 of the Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides information-only access points integrated within existing workforce services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of supernumerary agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Supernumerary agents (ordinary citizens with special training) accept claims in small isolated or rural localities, are authorized to complete required forms for claimants, receive $2.50 per claim, have no decision-making power, and must never express an opinion on the possibility of payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the strictly limited, form-filling assistance role and remuneration for occasional local agents and forbids advisory or adjudicative functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service unit composition and sizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Within decision-making offices, officers are organized into service units; each unit contains 15–20 persons headed by a unit supervisor responsible for organization, coordination and management under the Chief of Operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number of units per office varies (one to four) depending on population served and office position in hierarchy. Units are the primary locus of decision-making power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agents I and II decision roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Two classes of decision-making officers (Agents I and Agents II) exercise authority within units, generally working in pairs. Agent I can make decisions in obviously simple cases; Agent II handles more complex cases and serves as first-level reviewer for special situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents II bear primary responsibility; Agents I relieve workload by handling straightforward cases as defined by the UIC Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed clientele and personalized claimant service
rubrics_metrics.description: Each service unit has a fixed clientele (e.g., claimants whose SIN ends with certain digits or living in certain areas). Efforts are made to assign one agent permanently to a claimant to provide 'personalized claimant service'—replacing wicket/mail contact with personal face-to-face and telephone contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personalization is a central design goal of the unit principle and is cited as improving performance and simplifying hierarchical relationships; geographic and financial constraints may limit full implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit 'cells' for intensified personalization
rubrics_metrics.description: In small offices, units may be broken into 'cells' (one Agent II, one Agent I, and a clerk) working closely to achieve '100% personalization' by eliminating mail contact except for cheques and reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cells are an intensified organizational arrangement to maximize direct contact, but are subject to material constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment and training standard for Agents I
rubrics_metrics.description: Agents I are recruited almost entirely from UIC employees; training lasts two to three weeks during which they learn procedures and principles and work under close supervision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates expectation of internal promotion/career path and a short supervised training period before independent decision-making in simple cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment and training standard for Agents II
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximately one-quarter of Agents II are recruited from outside the UIC; their training period lasts four to six weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External recruitment is valued for bringing working-world experience; longer training reflects broader responsibilities and contributes to staff stability and job appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: General information channels for claimants
rubrics_metrics.description: Claimant information is provided via printed materials (newspapers, pamphlets, posters), audio-visual means (radio, TV, films, displays), and verbally by UIC employees. Some information is general (undifferentiated audience) while some is individual (in context of a claimant's claim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple channels are used to reach varied claimant populations; audio-visual displays are used where facilities allow; mass-media used primarily for practical notices and reminders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pamphlet set content and bilingual format
rubrics_metrics.description: A core set of eleven bilingual pamphlets (four procedural stage pamphlets, one on legal position 'Rights and obligations', six for specific claimant categories) plus additional bilingual leaflets and pamphlets (e.g., 'Your new job', 'Important notice to all employees').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pamphlets are prepared by PR division with technical supervision; they must balance simplicity (few technical terms) with fidelity to official terminology and provide accurate but not overly-detailed explanations; bilingual layout has one language per side of paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pamphlet distribution proportions and channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Printings are distributed by region: Ontario and Quebec 2/8 each, Atlantic/Prairie/Pacific 1/8 each, and 1/8 reserved in Ottawa; Regional Offices distribute to District Offices then satellite offices; pamphlets also made available in post offices and welfare/taxation offices; liaison officers may distribute to employers/unions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies intended allocation of printed informational materials to ensure regional availability and supplemental distribution points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language accessibility and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Most pamphlets are bilingual; Italian, Greek and Portuguese versions of seven pamphlets exist for immigrant claimants; a Chinese version was being prepared. However, application form, medical certificate and CMC registration form are available only in official languages. Verbal interactions may use interpreters or bilingual staff where available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses partial multilingual provision: translated explanatory materials are available locally, but key forms remain in English/French; interpreters or bilingual staff are used to bridge gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information clerks' duties and use of standard answers
rubrics_metrics.description: Information clerks answer claimant questions preferably in general terms based on system knowledge. Some offices maintain a book of standard answers to ensure uniformity. If claimant is receiving benefits, clerks can check payment state via a weekly videocassette statement; if file consultation is needed, calls are transferred to the responsible Agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clerks should provide uniform basic information and escalate to agents for file-specific or complex queries; information service can be overloaded in high-demand periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of mass-media and audiovisual techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Audio-visual displays are used in reception areas where space exists; mass-media (press, radio, TV, posters) are used for specific practical information (changes of address, opening times, cheque delivery arrangements) and to remind or explain aspects of procedure (e.g., Record of Employment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These techniques are targeted, practical, and supplementary to printed and in-person information; their role varies by office capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claimant's kit contents and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'claimant's kit' contains three forms (application for benefit, medical certificate, CMC registration form), the 'Rights and Obligations' pamphlet, sometimes 'How to complete your claimant's report' and other leaflets; the kit is packaged in a reply envelope addressed to issuing office and reminds the claimant to include SIN and ROE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kits are provided in-person or by mail and aim to give claimants the documents and explanatory material needed to initiate a claim and understand obligations; contents may vary by region.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information sessions for new claimants and signed obligation statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Some offices organize 15–20 minute information sessions (or AV presentations) for groups (~20) of recently-filed claimants to explain rights and obligations. At the end, claimants sign a statement acknowledging they have been informed about obligations (declare earnings, remain available, accept suitable employment, report unavailability days, actively search, keep job search record); the signed statement is attached to the file. The 'Rights and obligations' title in practice deals mainly with obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sessions and signed acknowledgements are used as procedural safeguards and to document claimant awareness of obligations; implications for disqualification are emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only application initiates the procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The application for benefit, submitted by an insured person using the appropriate form, is the only document that can initiate the UIC procedure (sec. 53 and 55(2) of the Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the formal trigger for administrative processing and the presumption that the applicant has minimum awareness of the scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application form format and mandatory completion rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The application is a two-page questionnaire (26 general questions plus four groups of special-situation questions). Most questions are set (yes/no) and must be answered. The claimant must answer all questions, sign the application, and indicate the official language preferred for dealings with UIC (sec. 55(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completeness, signature and language choice are mandatory procedural requirements; some answer options call for additional explanation on a separate sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required information elements on application
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must show: (a) length of last period of employment (to establish 8-week/20-week qualifying periods and benefit type), and reason for loss of employment (certain reasons may cause disqualification/penalties); (b) gross normal earnings and gross amount paid last week (used to set benefit rate) and amounts received on loss (severance/vacation) which may be deductible; (c) date/place of prior applications (to determine renewals); (d) Record of Employment details or explanation/attempts to obtain it (ROE is prima facie evidence of insurability, length, reason, earnings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the substantive evidentiary and eligibility items that must be reported and that will be used to compute entitlement or trigger penalties/deductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMC registration requirement and exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under sec. 55(7) most claimants are required to complete a Canada Manpower Centre (CMC) registration form at the time of application; exemptions include claimants applying for sickness/maternity/retirement benefits, those unemployed due to a labour dispute, short layoff or reduced to part-time with same employer, and union-hired employees under collective agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UIC forwards registration to CMC, which classifies job skills and experience and compiles monthly supply/demand statistics used by UIC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisors' limited scope when assisting claimants
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisors who help claimants complete applications are limited to providing indispensable explanations necessary to understand the form; they do not give opinions on the merits of an application to the claimant or to the adjudicating officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisors' role is clerical/explanatory only to preserve adjudicative neutrality and prevent influencing decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data-check procedure using regional payment records
rubrics_metrics.description: Clerks establishing claims access a complete record (stored on videocassettes) of benefits paid during the past year in the region to identify dates and lengths of previous benefits, determine renewals, or identify recent decisions that may affect the new claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results of the control are noted on a slip for the Agent; the check is intended to clarify whether prior decisions or recent benefits alter processing of the new claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: File opening contents and prompt processing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A file is opened under the claimant's SIN and should include the completed signed application, ROE (if provided), medical certificate (if applicable), CMC registration form, claimant's signed statement on rights/obligations, files on previous applications within past year, a slip on the state of any prior application, and an internal control slip. The application should be processed without delay (sec. 53(3) and 54(2) of the Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the documentary minimum for an adjudicator to make a decision and imposes statutory expectations for timely processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispatcher assignment and unit distribution process
rubrics_metrics.description: If submitted in person, the dispatcher records the claimant's name and SIN; the last digit of the SIN indicates the unit assignment. The dispatcher introduces the claimant to the assigned agent once available. Mail applications are data-checked, filed, and forwarded to the unit supervisor who distributes them among agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the operational intake workflow to ensure claims are routed to the correct service unit and agent for adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of decision-making responsibility (Agents II primary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision-making authority is delegated to Agents II (basic responsibility) with Agents I having subsidiary responsibility. Agents I are authorized by the UIC Manual to decide a variety of straightforward cases to reduce the Agents II workload.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies hierarchical responsibility, the delegation intent in sec.14(2) of the Act, and the practical office layout (Agents I desks near entrance; Agents II in second row) that supports these roles.
